drafts.title: Preserve and enhance overall driving enjoyment and confidence
drafts.description: Customers experience a smooth, engaging and confidence-inspiring drive in everyday and long-distance use: balanced ride comfort, composed handling and intuitive driving aids that make the car feel solid and pleasurable to drive.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 100-driver multi-road test (urban, B-roads, motorway) the successor scores ≥8.0/10 for overall driving enjoyment and ≥8.0/10 for confidence/stability; long-distance comfort score (2-hour continuous drive) ≥8.0/10; vehicle lateral handling (slalom consistency) within 5% of the best-in-class benchmark used in current BMW segment tests.
assumptions: Subjective scores come from a representative panel of 100 drivers in the EU; test methodology follows BMW customer-experience protocols.
Chassis and suspension development resources are available to maintain current BMW driving character.
uncertainties: Customer panel preferences may vary by market and trim; objective benchmarks may shift over time.

drafts.title: Deliver punchy, consistent engine power and seamless transmission response
drafts.description: Drivers feel immediate, linear throttle response and smooth, predictable gear changes with no hesitation, slipping or jerking across normal driving conditions and when accelerating or downshifting.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Base petrol trim 0–100 km/h ≤ 8.0 s; measured gearshift transient delay ≤ 0.25 s under typical acceleration; in a 1,000-gear-change durability fleet test <1% of shifts show a jerk event perceptible to drivers (rated ≥3/5 on jerk scale) and <0.5% of vehicles report transmission-related customer complaints in the first 12 months.
assumptions: Performance target for base petrol is realistic for successor platforms in 3–5 years.
Durability fleet tests replicate customer usage patterns and detect common transmission issues.
uncertainties: Electrified or alternative powertrain architectures may change the way acceleration and gearshift metrics are measured.
Exact 0–100 targets may need trim-level differentiation.

drafts.title: Brake behaviour must be progressive, predictable and tunable
drafts.description: Drivers experience a brake pedal that responds linearly and predictably across light and heavy braking, with regenerative braking levels that are adjustable and do not cause sudden grabs or delayed engagement.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Pedal travel vs deceleration shows a linear relationship with correlation r ≥ 0.95 in standardized tests; regenerative braking can be set to at least three levels and users can select a smooth default; fleet durability test of 10,000 stops records <0.5% incidents of sudden 'grab' or unresponsive braking reported by test drivers.
assumptions: Brake feel tuning will combine hydraulic and regenerative systems on electrified variants.
Standardized tests reflect customer perception of progressive braking.
uncertainties: Precise quantification of 'grab' is subjective; acceptance uses a mix of objective measurement and driver panel scoring.

drafts.title: Maintain or improve ride comfort while preserving nimble handling
drafts.description: Customers experience a comfortable, composed ride over rough surfaces without sacrificing the car's agility and steering feedback on twisty roads.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In the customer ride/handling benchmark (100 drivers) average ride comfort score ≥8.0/10 and steering/handling score ≥8.0/10; body acceleration RMS measured on defined road profiles is reduced by ≥10% versus the current model.
assumptions: Objective vibration measurements are correlated to subjective comfort scores.
Chassis architecture allows simultaneous improvements in damping and agility.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between sporty handling and softer ride may vary by customer; tuning may require multiple suspension options.

drafts.title: Seats must be supportive, comfortable for long trips and robust in quality
drafts.description: Occupants experience seats that provide effective lumbar and lateral support for long drives, are easy to adjust, and remain free of squeaks, creasing and electrical faults over normal ownership periods.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: 2-hour endurance seating test average comfort score ≥8.0/10 (100-person panel); lumbar support with at least 4-way adjustability; manufacturing quality target: <0.5% seat-related faults (stitching, creaks, electric faults) in first 12 months across production sample.
assumptions: Endurance and quality tests replicate typical owner usage for 3 years.
Adjustability is implemented in a way accessible to customers of different heights.
uncertainties: Perception of comfort is subjective; targets combine objective durability data and subjective scoring.

drafts.title: Restore physical controls for core functions and ensure media/ audio basics work reliably
drafts.description: Customers can adjust essential functions (climate, fan, temperature, audio volume/source) with dedicated physical buttons/knobs quickly and without looking, while still offering a large central display for secondary features; playing music from USB storage is supported and audio sound is natural unless the driver explicitly chooses synthetic augmentation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Dedicated physical controls present for HVAC (driver & passenger), fan and audio volume/source; tests show these can be operated without visual attention in ≤1.5 s; at least one front USB port supports mass-storage playback and is labelled for media; by default no synthetic engine pops are played through speakers (user opt-in allowed); audio system user-satisfaction ≥8.0/10 in listening tests.
assumptions: Physical controls are ergonomically integrated without cluttering the cabin.
Audio evaluations are performed with representative music tracks and in-vehicle listening tests.
uncertainties: Some customers prefer touchscreen-only layouts; requirement aims to satisfy majority safety/usability concerns.

drafts.title: Infotainment and connected software must be reliable, intuitive and maintain feature availability
drafts.description: Customers experience an infotainment system that is responsive, rarely crashes, keeps features available after updates and offers reliable connected services and dealer support if problems occur.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System crash/lockup rate <0.1 incidents per 1,000 vehicle-hours in pre-production validation and early fleet; post-update feature-regression incidents <0.5% across fleet during first 24 months; connected-services customer-satisfaction ≥8.0/10 (EU study benchmark).
assumptions: Improved QA processes and update procedures will be implemented to avoid regressions.
Connected services score target is comparable to other class leaders in the EU market.
uncertainties: Third-party services and network dependencies may affect connected-services availability.
Exact numeric targets require agreement with software/OTA strategy.

drafts.title: Provide full sat‑nav functionality without forcing app registration and ensure reliable routing
drafts.description: Drivers can use full navigation functionality out of the box without mandatory app registration or paid activation and navigation works reliably with clear routing and voice guidance.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: All core navigation features available and usable without app registration; offline map routing available for EU countries and a 500 km route is calculated within ≤5 s on the vehicle hardware; voice guidance and turn-by-turn rerouting operate correctly in ≥99% of tested navigation scenarios.
assumptions: Sufficient onboard map/data storage or hybrid offline-online approach will be provided.
Regulatory or commercial constraints do not mandate app-based features for certain services.
uncertainties: Some advanced services (real-time traffic) may still require connectivity; objective is that core routing and guidance are available without app login.

drafts.title: Deliver usable boot space and reliable tailgate operation for everyday practicality
drafts.description: Customers can load common luggage and groceries without compromise from hybrid packaging, and the tailgate opens/closes reliably with convenient internal controls.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured boot capacity ≥380 litres for non-electrified variants (VDA method) and ≥300 litres usable for electrified/hybrid variants; electric tailgate with internal close button included on at least mid trims; tailgate operation reliability ≥99% over 10,000 cycles in durability testing; common luggage-fit test passed in ≥95% of cases.
assumptions: Packaging improvements and battery layout for hybrids will allow the stated usable volumes.
Electric tailgate hardware will be validated for durability in typical use.
uncertainties: Exact boot volumes will vary with trim (spare wheel, sound systems); targets apply to standard configuration.

drafts.title: Keys and driver-profile features must feel premium and work reliably
drafts.description: Customers experience high quality tactile keys and reliable digital-key features that remember driver settings and do not cause unexpected locking or alarm events.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Physical key build quality target: >95% positive tactile satisfaction in customer evaluation; digital-key and profile recall success ≥99% within 2 s of unlocking in bench and vehicle tests; incidents of unexpected re-locking or alarm triggering <0.5% in first 12 months fleet data.
assumptions: Key hardware and software integration will be validated in pre-production and early fleet.
Metrics combine subjective evaluation and objective functional tests.
uncertainties: Smartphone-based digital-key behavior depends on phone OS versions and user settings.

drafts.title: Improve exterior mirrors and visibility to remove blind spots and reduce night glare
drafts.description: Drivers experience improved visibility from exterior mirrors with minimized blind spots and reduced interior reflection/glare at night so mirror use feels safe and reliable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: External mirror field-of-view meets or exceeds current class benchmark (ISO/Euro NCAP mirror visibility tests) and night-glare tests show no significant interior reflections that impair view in ≥95% of laboratory/night scenarios; all expected mirror functions (adjust, heat, folding) operate correctly in ≥99% of vehicles in QC testing.
assumptions: Mirror geometry and coatings can be optimized within existing packaging and regulatory constraints.
Lab night-glare tests replicate common cabin lighting conditions.
uncertainties: Perception of blind spots varies by driver; objective tests reduce but may not eliminate every customer complaint.

drafts.title: Fit tyres that balance low noise, strong wet grip and robust durability
drafts.description: Customers notice quieter tyres with confident grip in wet weather and acceptable durability for European conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Selected OEM tyre specification yields exterior tyre noise ≤72 dB at 80 km/h (ISO test) and wet braking performance from 80 km/h to 0 km/h ≤32 m in standardized tests; tyre-related roadside incidents in first 12 months <1% of fleet.
assumptions: Targets are achievable with mainstream premium tyre suppliers and appropriate wheel/tire fitment per trim.
Durability testing reflects typical EU road conditions including potholes.
uncertainties: Extreme road conditions and aftermarket tyre choices can affect noise and grip outcomes.

drafts.title: Improve exterior quality and lighting so the car looks premium and is usable at night
drafts.description: Customers experience high-quality exterior fit & finish and lighting that provides good night visibility without causing nuisance glare or reflections.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Exterior build-quality complaints (paint, trim, panel-fit) reduced by ≥80% compared with the current model in early ownership feedback; headlamp performance meets or exceeds applicable UNECE standards and customer night-visibility score ≥8.0/10 in usability tests.
assumptions: Improved quality control and supplier processes will reduce visible defects.
Lighting improvements may require revised headlamp modules but will comply with regulations.
uncertainties: Supplier variability and production ramps can temporarily affect early quality.

drafts.title: Offer competitive electric range for battery-electric variants
drafts.description: When choosing a BEV variant, customers experience ranges that meet or exceed competitor expectations for mid-range and long-range buyers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Mid-trim BEV WLTP range ≥350 km; long-range BEV WLTP range ≥500 km (where a long-range option is offered); real-world town/motorway mixed-cycle range within ±15% of WLTP for typical driving profiles.
assumptions: Battery energy-density and vehicle efficiency trends continue to improve over the next 3–5 years enabling these ranges.
WLTP remains the standard reference for marketing-range comparisons in target markets.
uncertainties: Actual range depends on driving style, options, climate and payload; targets represent reasonable mid-term expectations.
